families.label: Transport control → proxy warmness → high accuracy
families.plain_language: A nearby Renyi-warm witness is enough for accuracy under the same implemented probability kernel; expected cost requires a different, actual-input bound.
families.do_not_conflate: W2 proximity is not Renyi warmness; the actual law is not its proxy; TV closeness alone does not transfer unbounded costs.

families.label: Reflection coupling and discrete modified-L2 decay
families.plain_language: Use a conditional-expectation projection to separate macro and micro modes. An involution couples them; a half-turn estimate and corrected energy propagate microscopic damping to macroscopic control.
families.do_not_conflate: The conditional PDMP, discrete augmented chain, and continuous-time Langevin theorem have different operators and domains. Reuse requires adapters, not renaming a generator.

families.label: Metric gradient flow → dissipation → exponential decay
families.plain_language: The state space changes, but the same proof skeleton can survive: choose an energy and a metric, identify its metric gradient, write energy dissipation, then use a PL-shaped inequality to turn dissipation into exponential convergence.
reading_order: gradient flow gives an energy-dissipation identity
metric PL closes the scalar differential inequality
only then specialize to Euclidean, Riemannian, or Wasserstein geometry
families.do_not_conflate: Wasserstein/Otto calculus needs rigorous first-variation and flow hypotheses; W2 is not globally a classical smooth finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold.

families.label: Second-order curvature → first-order/growth controls
families.plain_language: Strong convexity is not merely a faster convergence assumption. It is a lower-curvature statement that produces a quadratic lower model and, after the right geometry is chosen, often yields growth or PL-like coercivity.

compiled_substrate_bindings.role: Compiled Euclidean first-order quadratic lower model produced by strong convexity.
compiled_substrate_bindings.truth_boundary: This module is a substrate for the Euclidean curvature-to-growth pattern only. It does not certify Riemannian, Wasserstein, Bakry-Emery, PL, Poincare, or LSI arrows.

reading_order: Wasserstein geodesic convexity or Bakry-Emery curvature in their own settings
derive only the coercivity statement justified by that setting
families.do_not_conflate: Euclidean Hessian bounds, geodesic convexity, displacement convexity, and Bakry-Emery curvature are related patterns but not interchangeable hypotheses.

families.label: PL / LSI mirror: objective gap versus gradient dissipation
families.plain_language: Optimization PL bounds the objective gap by a squared gradient. For Langevin, LSI bounds KL by relative Fisher information, which is the squared Wasserstein gradient norm of KL in the smooth formal picture. Both turn the same dissipation identity into exponential gap decay.
reading_order: identify its exact dissipation / metric-gradient norm
state the PL-shaped coercivity with source normalization
families.do_not_conflate: LSI is a functional inequality for measures/densities, not literally the Euclidean PL theorem; constants and factors of two depend on normalization.

families.label: Poincare / chi-square mirror: quadratic gap versus Dirichlet dissipation
families.plain_language: For density ratio rho, chi-square is the squared L2 distance of rho from 1. Poincare controls this quadratic gap by Dirichlet energy, and reversible semigroup dissipation then gives exponential chi-square decay.
reading_order: chi-square as an L2 density gap
Poincare as coercivity of the Dirichlet form
families.do_not_conflate: Poincare/chi-square and LSI/KL are parallel dissipation templates but different inequalities and generally different strengths.

families.label: Quadratic regularization: proximal minimizer or Gibbs draw
families.plain_language: Optimization and sampling can consume the same regularized energy differently: one chooses its minimizer, the other samples from its normalized exponential.
reading_order: separate existence, normalization, and invariance obligations
families.do_not_conflate: Sharing an energy does not make the proximal map and restricted Gaussian oracle equivalent outputs.

families.label: Conditional influence and local-to-global mixing
families.plain_language: Control dependence under all feasible pinnings, then lift local spectral or factorization bounds to a global sampler. Reuse matrix/probability algebra without identifying this condition with strong convexity.
reading_order: finite support and positive conditioning events
families.do_not_conflate: One covariance matrix is not spectral independence; neither is Euclidean strong convexity or generating-polynomial log-concavity without a proved bridge.

families.label: Target-invariance correction
families.plain_language: Construct a target-invariant transition from a proposal; density and finite-state adapters share one accepted-flux idea.
families.do_not_conflate: No mixing theorem or universal efficiency improvement.

families.label: High-dimensional scaling and diffusion limits
families.plain_language: Transport the analysis only through a proved asymptotic limit with its own clock.
families.do_not_conflate: Weak convergence is not finite-time uniform mixing.

families.label: Augmented state and marginal invariance
families.plain_language: Prove invariance on an enlarged space and recover the desired marginal.
families.do_not_conflate: HMC is not always nonreversible; geometry must preserve volume conventions.

families.label: Ideal versus implemented Markov kernels
families.plain_language: Keep perturbation error and ideal mixing as separately proved terms.
families.do_not_conflate: Fixed-step numerical samplers can retain a target bias.

families.label: Gaussian symmetries through actual pushforwards
families.plain_language: Preserve a genuine Gaussian law by a symmetry and carry that symmetry through the actual measurable generative map; concentration calibration remains a separate proof.
reading_order: distinct covariance calibration and failure boundaries
families.do_not_conflate: Rotating an arbitrary mu with a Gaussian does not preserve mu product gamma: at theta=pi/2 a non-Gaussian or noncentered mu is swapped with gamma. PBPS avoids that by fixing the arbitrary input. Gaussian reflection and rotation are different maps; reflection involutivity is not a generic rotation conclusion. Identically distributed centered anisotropic Gaussian copies may retain rotation invariance, but isotropic sharp coefficient1/2 in the given metric cannot be inferred. No PBPS reflection theorem implies the sharp concentration bound, nonexplosion, hypocoercivity, actual algorithm or query costs. No certified functor/equivalence or solid Lean dependency is claimed.

families.label: Function entropy and coordinate perturbation energy
families.plain_language: Build entropy control on actual independent coordinates, then separately prove law and local-energy limits before changing spaces.
reading_order: Actual finite Bool count full-flip energy inequality
Compact real, finite Hilbert and noncompact cutoff extension (open)
families.do_not_conflate: No arbitrary dependent Boolean/Gibbs law, modified LSI jump entropy, covariance mismatch, noncompact extension without limits, canonical RN differentiation from AE equality, T2/W2/main/composition or unbounded cost transfer. CLT law convergence alone does not imply flip-energy convergence; the map is many-to-one and no theorem equivalence is asserted.

families.label: Gaussian oracle hardness through hidden information and tests
families.plain_language: Specify what an exact query reveals, keep the target test separate, then join both estimates under the same accuracy and budget contract.
